next_question: Can an estimator with sufficient sensitivity — such as a plug-in transition-matrix KL divergence estimator (D_KL(P(Y|Z,A) || P(Y|Z)) computed directly on the stochastic SPA's empirical transitions), a KSG CMI variant with k=10 or k=20 to increase neighborhood resolution, or a permutation test conditioned on (state, action) strata — detect the demonstrated 1.52-bit CMI signal while preserving |shuffled-action null_mean| < 0.1 bits at N=5000, thereby resolving whether the insensitivity is specific to KSG k=5 and LR chi2-per-state, or fundamental to discrete CMI estimation on 12-state SPAs?
why_next: Both KSG CMI (k=5) and LR (chi2-per-state) fail C3 on the stochastic SPA despite audit-confirmed true CMI of 1.52 bits (3x above the 0.5 threshold). KSG returns K3=0.000560 (893x below threshold), LR returns K3=0.103695 (4.8x below threshold, identical to degenerate deterministic SPA baseline). Null centering works for both (C1 passes with 8-22x margin), confirming the null framework is sound. The failure is estimator sensitivity, not SPA design. The next experiment must determine whether this insensitivity is estimator-specific (KSG k=5 too coarse for 12-state discrete; LR ignores history by construction) or fundamental to all discrete CMI estimation on this SPA class. A transition-matrix KL estimator bypasses CMI estimation entirely. KSG k=10/20 tests neighborhood resolution. These are materially orthogonal approaches that could each independently resolve the question.

do_not_assume: KSG CMI and LR are useless for all CMI estimation. They achieve null centering (genuine methodological advance) but are insensitive to the specific signal on this SPA class. Different k values, distance encodings, or estimator families may succeed.

The 1.52-bit true CMI should be easy to detect. Discrete 12-state data with k=5 neighbors presents specific resolution challenges that may not apply to larger state spaces or continuous representations.

Null centering by near-zero output (KSG null_std=0.000187) is equivalent to unbiased estimation. It is a conservative defense against false positives but comes at the cost of sensitivity. The estimator is effectively a constant function for this input range.

Global shuffle deviation invalidates C1 results. The C1 margin is 8-22x below threshold; even with within-session shuffle correction, C1 would likely still pass. The deviation must be disclosed but does not change the verdict.

Missing baseline execution (4/7 baselines) invalidates the experiment. The two executed estimators (KSG, LR) are the primary test targets. The missing baselines would replicate parent PMI bias (~0.41-0.70 bits) but their absence does not affect the C1/C3 verdict.

The frozen FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING closes the C-WEB-DYNAMICS claim or the Physics lane. It closes only the KSG k=5 and LR chi2-per-state pathways on this specific SPA class. The SPA design is valid; alternative estimators remain untested.

Production Web transitions generalize from this synthetic SPA. The 12-state SPA has hash routing, 4 candidates per (state,action), no anti-bot, auth, visual complexity, or stochastic production dynamics.

recommended_action: Design a new experiment testing alternative estimators on the validated stochastic SPA (I(Y;A|Z)=1.52 bits). Priority order: (1) plug-in transition-matrix KL divergence estimator -- directly computes D_KL(P(Y|Z,A) || P(Y|Z)) on empirical transitions, bypassing CMI estimation entirely; (2) KSG CMI with k=10 or k=20 -- tests whether neighborhood resolution is the binding constraint; (3) permutation test conditioned on (state, action) strata -- tests whether action-label permutation within state breaks the signal. All must satisfy C1 (|null_mean| < 0.1) and C3 (positive_control_k3 >= 0.5, p <= 0.001) on the same stochastic SPA at N=5000 with within-session shuffle (correcting the global shuffle deviation). If all alternative estimators also fail C3, the Physics lane should pivot to fundamentally different detection paradigms (entropy rate, channel capacity, causal discovery) or move to production Web data, as the estimator-insensitivity pathway would be exhausted.
